Q166646.label: Ramsay MacDonald
Q166646.desc: British prime minister in 1924 and 1929 to 1935 (1866–1937)
Q166646.summary: James Ramsay MacDonald was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom twice, first briefly in 1924 and again from 1929 to 1935. The first two of his governments belonged to the Labour Party: a minority Labour government for nine months in 1924, making him the first Labour Prime Minister in British history, and the second between 1929 and 1931. In 1931, MacDonald was expelled from the Labour Party; after, he formed a National Government dominated by the Conservative Party and supported by only a few Labour members. His premiership then lasted until 1935.

Q7232758.label: 1945 Portuguese legislative election
Q7232758.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Portugal on 18 November 1945. Following reforms introduced by António de Oliveira Salazar, they were the first elections in the Estado Novo to allow opposition parties. The Movement of Democratic Unity was formed by opposition activists, but alongside all opposition candidates, they withdrew from the election before polling day, alleging electoral fraud. As a result, only candidates of the National Union contested the election.

Q613622.label: 1992 Slovenian parliamentary election
Q613622.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Slovenia on 6 and 10 December 1992. These were the first legislative elections to the National Assembly after the rename of the Assembly of the Republic of Slovenia in December 1991 and the first elections in independent Slovenia. The result was a victory for the Liberal Democratic Party, which won 22 of the 90 seats.

Q57590.label: Mykola Azarov
Q57590.summary: Mykola Yanovych Azarov is a Russo-Ukrainian politician who was the Prime Minister of Ukraine from 11 March 2010 to 27 January 2014. He was the First Vice Prime Minister and Finance Minister from 2002 to 2005 and again from 2006 to 2007. Azarov also served ex officio as an acting prime minister in the First Yanukovych Government when Viktor Yanukovych ran for president at first and then upon the resignation of his government.

Q4173046.label: Yevpatoria assault
Q4173046.img: Walki uliczne w mieście na Krymie (2-840).jpg
Q4173046.summary: The Yevpatoria assault was an amphibious assault during World War II by Soviet marine battalion on 5 January 1942 at Yevpatoria aiming at diverting part of German troops attacking Sevastopol and the Kerch Peninsula.

Q4084470.label: Bereznegovatoye–Snigirevka offensive
Q4084470.desc: part of Dnieper–Carpathian offensive on the Eastern Front of WW2
Q4084470.summary: The Bereznegovatoye–Snigirevka offensive operation, known on the German side as The second winter battle of the 6th Army between the Dnieper, Ingulets and Bug, was an offensive operation conducted in southern Ukraine by the Soviet 3rd Ukrainian Front against the German 6th Army and Romanian 3rd Army of Army Group A, in March 1944. It was part of the second stage of the strategic Dnieper-Carpathian Offensive.

Q123285238.label: Red Sea crisis
Q123285238.desc: main part of the Houthi involvement in the Israel–Hamas war
Q123285238.summary: The Red Sea crisis is an ongoing armed conflict and maritime crisis instigated by the Houthis, an armed group in Yemen fighting a civil war against the country's internationally recognized government. The Houthis began launching missiles and armed drones at Israel in response to the Gaza war, and have seized or attacked dozens of merchant and naval vessels travelling through the Red Sea which they claimed are linked to Israel. These actions provoked a military response from Israel, as well as the United States and the United Kingdom.

Q136202486.label: Al-Farabi School Bombing
Q136202486.desc: school bombing by the IDF on 7 September 2025
Q136202486.summary: The Al-Farabi School Bombing occurred in the early morning hours of September 7, 2025, in a southwestern part of Gaza City, near the al-Yarmouk Stadium. The attack killed eight people including several children in the school, which was being used as a shelter. A witness reported that the strike was carried out using two rockets.

Q322294.label: statism
Q322294.desc: doctrine that the political authority of the state is legitimate to some degree
Q322294.summary: In political science, statism or etatism is the doctrine that the political authority of the state is legitimate to some degree. This may include economic and social policy, especially in regard to taxation and the means of production.
